title: GitHub - mrscraper-com/mrscraper-mcp: Official MrScraper MCP server: Scraper API for HTML, Markdown, and screenshots, web search, and account usage for AI agents.
snippet:
An MCP server exposing the seven MrScraper services through hosted HTTP or local stdio.
## Overview
Seven services share the same descriptions, parameter meanings, and defaults across the CLI, SDKs, and integrations. Names, types, authentication, and code examples follow each surface's conventions. See the [API Reference](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/overview).
| Service | Public name | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Status | `status` | Return the raw account status API response without summarizing, redacting body fields, or adding calculated fields. |
| Scrape HTML | `scrapeHtml` | Retrieve the raw HTML of a page. Browser rendering is optional. |
| Scrape Markdown | `scrapeMarkdown` | Retrieve a page as Markdown. Including HTML also enables browser rendering and returns both outputs as JSON. |
| Get screenshot | `getScreenshot` | Capture a base64 screenshot of the full page or top viewport. Browser rendering is always enabled. |
| Scrape brand | `scrapeBrand` | Extract a website's colors, typography, logos, and social links as JSON. |
| Scrape JSON | `scrapeJson` | Extract structured JSON from a page using a natural-language prompt. Append Json Schema: and a JSON schema to shape the output. |
| Web search | `webSearch` | Search the web and return ranked results with titles, URLs, descriptions, and sources. |
## Installation
The hosted server requires an MCP client with Streamable HTTP support. Local execution requires Node.js 20 or newer.
Configure the hosted endpoint in your MCP client:
```
{ "mcpServers": { "mrscraper": { "url": "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp" } } }
```
For local stdio, configure the client to start `npx -y @mrscraper/mcp@latest`. The full configuration is in Integration features.
## Authentication
Obtain an API key from [the MrScraper app](https://app.mrscraper.com/api-tokens). API key used to authenticate the request.
The hosted server supports browser sign-in through OAuth 2.1. Approve `account:read` for status and `scrape:read` for all six scraping/search tools. Connections that already hold `scrape:read` keep working; others must reconnect and approve it for scraping/search.
Clients without OAuth can send an API key as `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN`. Local stdio reads `MRSCRAPER_API_KEY`, then `MRSCRAPER_API_TOKEN`. Tools do not accept tokens as arguments.
```
{
"mcpServers": {
"mrscraper": {
"url": "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp",
"headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" }
}
}
}
```

# MCP Server
Access MrScraper’s web scraping API via a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to enable AI agents to fetch and extract web data securely.
Use MrScraper’s web scraping API through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to let AI agents discover, fetch, and extract web data in real time. This cloud-hosted MCP server integrates directly with MrScraper, enabling secure, scalable scraping workflows without local setup or infrastructure management.
## Features
### AI Scraping

### Scraper Execution
### Bulk Scraping
### Results Management
### Rotating Proxies
### Cloud MCP Server
## Installation

To use the MrScraper MCP server, you'll need:
1. [A MrScraper account](https://v3.app.mrscraper.com/auth/login)
2. [MrScraper Account API Key](/docs/getting-started/api-token#generating-an-api-token)

title: @mrscraper/mcp
Choose an Agent Framework for a Web Data Application
snippet:
For MrScraper, there are a few documented paths:
- **The [MrScraper MCP server](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/getting-started/mcp-server).** It offers `scraperAPI`, `webSearch` and `status` tools to any MCP client. It runs hosted at `https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp` or locally.
- **The [LangChain integration](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/integrations/langchain).** The `langchain-mrscraper` package gives LangChain and LangGraph agents eight ready-made tools.
- **The [REST API](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/api/overview), [Python SDK](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/integrations/python) or [Node.js SDK](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/integrations/node).** You wrap these in your own typed tools. Since every framework below supports MCP, the MCP server works with all of them. Custom tools give you more control over inputs, outputs and errors.

| Framework | Deployment paths named in the docs |
|---|---|
| LangGraph | Your own servers, or LangSmith Deployment for long-running, stateful workflows |
| OpenAI Agents SDK | Your own infrastructure; it is a library you run |
| Google ADK | Containers on your own infrastructure, or Agent Runtime, Cloud Run or GKE on Google Cloud |
| CrewAI | Your own infrastructure, or the CrewAI Enterprise console |
| Mastra | Inside TypeScript apps such as Next.js, Express or Hono, plus Mastra's deploy options |
| Claude Agent SDK | A process you operate; the SDK runs the Claude Code binary |

Here is the hosted MCP server in the OpenAI Agents SDK. The key comes from an environment variable and is sent as a bearer token, which is the API key option the MrScraper MCP docs describe.
python
```python
import os
from agents import Agent, Runner
from agents.mcp import MCPServerStreamableHttp
async def run_task(prompt: str):
async with MCPServerStreamableHttp(
name="mrscraper",
params={
"url": "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp",
"headers": {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['MRSCRAPER_API_KEY']}"},
},
) as server:
agent = Agent(
name="Release checker",
instructions="Use only the given URLs. Quote the page for every field.",
mcp_servers=[server],
)
return await Runner.run(agent, prompt, max_turns=10)
```
And here is the same server in the Claude Agent SDK:
python
```python
import os
from claude_agent_sdk import ClaudeAgentOptions
options = ClaudeAgentOptions(
mcp_servers={
"mrscraper": {
"type": "http",
"url": "https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp",
"headers": {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['MRSCRAPER_API_KEY']}"},
}

snippet:
# Nous-approved MCP catalog entry.
# Presence in this directory = approval. Merged via PR review.
manifest_version: 1
name: mrscraper
description: Retrieve web pages, search Google, and check account usage.
source: https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/getting-started/mcp-server
# Official hosted Streamable HTTP server. Its 401 challenge advertises MCP
# protected-resource metadata and an OAuth authorization server with dynamic
# client registration and PKCE. No local package or static key is required.
transport:
type: http
url: https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp
auth:
type: oauth
# The server currently exposes scraperAPI, webSearch, and status.
# With no fixed tool filter, installation lets
# users choose among the tools available at connection time.
suggest:
keywords:
- mrscraper
- mr scraper
hosts:
- mrscraper.com
post_install: |
On first connection, Hermes opens MrScraper browser sign-in. Approve access
and start a new session to load its tools. If sign-in does not start, run:
hermes mcp login mrscraper
The server provides scraperAPI (HTML, Markdown, or screenshots),
webSearch (Google results), and status (account usage and quota).
For managed scrapers, reruns, and stored results, use the MrScraper dashboard.
Review or change enabled tools with:
hermes mcp configure mrscraper
Requests send target URLs and search queries to
MrScraper's cloud service. Scraping and search can consume account tokens;
use status to inspect your remaining quota before large jobs.

title: Use MrScraper MCP to Compare Public SaaS Pricing and Plan Limits
snippet:
An MCP SaaS pricing comparison uses an AI client, such as Claude Code, to collect official pricing and help pages through MrScraper's MCP tools. The client then turns each page into structured, cited rows. You compare plans only where units match, and you mark every unpublished price or limit as unknown.

It works in four steps: you define the question, MrScraper MCP collects the official pages, your AI client extracts facts into a fixed schema, and you build the comparison from those facts. MCP handles collection. The comparison rules are yours, and they live in your prompt and your review.

Connect MrScraper's hosted MCP server to your AI client, then ask the client to call `scraperAPI` on each approved URL and extract facts into your schema. Each call returns the page content in the same response. Check the response before you trust any fact taken from it.
### **scraperAPI output and response validation**
MrScraper documents a hosted MCP endpoint at `https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp` with OAuth 2.1 sign-in. In Claude Code, add it like this:
bash
```bash
claude mcp add \
--transport http \
--scope user \
mrscraper https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp
```
Open `/mcp` in Claude Code to sign in. Other clients, including Claude Desktop, Cursor and VS Code, use the same URL. The [MrScraper MCP documentation](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/getting-started/mcp-server) lists the setup for each one.
The server offers three tools: `scraperAPI` to collect a page, `webSearch` to search Google and `status` to check account usage. For this task, `scraperAPI` does almost all the work.

title: Authenticate Web Data Tools for AI Agents Without Exposing Secrets
snippet:
1. **Your backend owns the key.** Your server holds a MrScraper API token. The agent calls your tools, and your server calls MrScraper.
2. **Each user connects their own account.** A person signs in to MrScraper through their MCP client, such as Claude Code or Codex. The client handles the sign-in, and the agent uses that person's access.

Use OAuth when |
|---|---|
| Your app calls MrScraper on its own behalf | A person connects their own MrScraper account |
| The call runs on your server, a job runner or CI | The call runs from that person's MCP client |
| One account pays for and owns the usage | Each person's usage should stay on their account |
| You control where the key is stored | You do not want anyone to copy or paste a key |

### **OAuth for people using MCP clients**
The hosted [MrScraper MCP server](https://docs.mrscraper.com/docs/getting-started/mcp-server) at `https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp` supports OAuth 2.1. The client opens a browser, the person signs in, and no key is copied anywhere.
To add it in Claude Code:
bash
```bash
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user mrscraper https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp
```
To add it in Codex:
bash
```bash
codex mcp add mrscraper --url https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp
```
OAuth access uses scopes:
- **`scrape:read`** covers the `scraperAPI` and `webSearch` tools.
- **`account:read`** covers the `status` tool. If a client calls a tool without the right scope, the server refuses it with a 403 `insufficient_scope` error. Grant only the scopes a person needs.
### **When a client does not support OAuth**
Some MCP clients cannot do the browser sign-in. For those, the MCP server accepts an API key as a bearer token in the `Authorization` header. If you run it locally over stdio, it reads the key from the `MRSCRAPER_API_KEY` environment variable.
Point the client at the variable name, not the value, when it lets you. Codex supports this with a flag:
bash
```bash
codex mcp add mrscraper --url https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp \
--bearer-token-env-var MRSCRAPER_API_KEY
```
If a client config file must hold the key, keep that file out of version control and readable only by you.

There are two kinds of access in an agent app:
- **User access** answers "who is asking?" Your app's own login handles this.
- **Service access** answers "what is allowed to call MrScraper?" Your server's MrScraper token handles this. Never pass the service token to a user, and never let a user's request choose which token to use.
